_readme: Topps' own Pokemon trading cards, from pricecharting.com.
Written by scripts/sync-topps-top.mjs from the pages sync-graded-top.mjs
already cached. NO NETWORK: see that script's header before adding one.
WHAT THESE CARDS ARE. Topps printed Pokemon TRADING cards under licence
around 1999-2004: anime and movie stills on card stock, with no HP, no
attacks and no energy cost. They are not Pokemon TCG cards and cannot be
played with. PriceCharting files and prices them under Pokemon anyway,
which is why they turn up in this site's site-wide rankings.
WHAT THE NUMBERS ARE. PriceCharting's Ungraded, Grade 9 and PSA 10 price
guide values, computed by their algorithm from completed eBay sales and
their own marketplace. NOT a marketplace price, NOT a live listing and NOT
an auction result, and no page may describe them as any of those.
`rank` IS AN IDENTIFIER, NOT A RANKING. It is a row's position in the
union of the two candidate windows. The rankings are `rawOrder` and
`psaOrder`, which are arrays of those rank numbers.
`rows` PER SET IS PRODUCT RECORDS, NOT CARDS. 2000 Topps Chrome is 604
rows and 151 numbered cards, because the plain card and its Sparkle, Tekno
and Spectra parallels are four products against one number. `numbers` is
the distinct collector numbers. Neither is a print-run fact.
A SNAPSHOT. `checked` is the day the crawl read these pages, borrowed from
data/top-graded.json because they are the same crawl.
NOTHING HERE IS PUBLISHABLE UNTIL verify-topps-top.mjs HAS RUN. The td ids
on a product page mean different grades than the ones on a listing page,
so a single read cannot be trusted. See data/top-graded-PLAN.md, trap 4.
measurement: PriceCharting ungraded, Grade 9 and PSA 10 price guide values

verify.method: re-read the Ungraded, Grade 9 and PSA 10 columns from each product page, mapping columns by <th> label

excluded.name: Charizard [Rainbow Foil] #6
excluded.public: the PSA 10 guide value moved between the two reads, so we hold two correct readings of it rather than one
excluded.why: NOT a parse failure. The console listing was crawled on 22 August 2026 and the product page read the same morning, and PriceCharting's own "dollar change from last update" on that product page's PSA 10 cell says the value rose by $779.76: 3,908.08 - 779.76 = 3,128.32, the listing figure, to the cent. The same row's other two columns agreed and reconcile the same way (Ungraded 87.49 to 88.11 on a change of +0.62, Grade 9 787.25 to 787.41 on a change of +0.16), which is what a single new PSA 10 sale looks like against two columns that did not move. Across all 177 rows and all three price columns, 458 readings have a figure on both page types: 449 are identical to the cent and the other 9 all reconcile against the change PriceCharting itself reports, with none left over, so the column mapping is demonstrably right on every row. This is the only reading on the file outside the verifier tolerance of 0.15: +24.93%, against +1.06% for the next largest, #2 Charizard [Sparkle] #6. Two correctly read figures this far apart still give no basis for printing either one, so the PSA 10 figure is excluded and this card cannot appear on the list ranked by it. It stood 56th in that order. Its other columns are gated separately: its Ungraded figure agreed, and it was never a candidate for the raw hundred.
